description: What the agent may do with the content. Seeded from RSL 1.0 AI-use vocabulary (canonical source for ai-* and search tokens) and extended with established IP/copyright terms for non-AI domains (music, 3D, CAD, stock media, datasets).

tokens.description: All uses — shorthand for permitting or prohibiting the entire set of defined functions.
tokens.notes: Mutually exclusive with any other token in the same permitted[] or prohibited[] list. When in prohibited[], no use is allowed without an explicit scoped offer.

tokens.description: All AI uses — shorthand covering ai-train, ai-input, ai-index, and tts.
tokens.notes: Subset of all. When a publisher permits ai-all, ai-train, ai-input, ai-index, and tts are each individually permitted. Individual tokens in the same list take precedence for specificity.

tokens.description: Use as machine learning or AI model training data: pre-training, fine-tuning, RLHF, distillation.
tokens.notes: Alias train-ai is from IETF AIPREF draft. Does not cover inference-time use (see ai-input). Covered by ai-all.

tokens.description: Use as input to an AI inference call: retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), grounding, agent context, summarization, and completion.
tokens.notes: Alias generative-ai is widely used in industry; ai-input is the RSL 1.0 canonical term. Covers any use where the content is provided as context to a live AI inference call, including agentic workflows and multi-turn conversations. Does not cover training (see ai-train). Covered by ai-all.

tokens.description: Build a retrieval index for AI-powered search: vector embedding, semantic search index construction, nearest-neighbour retrieval.
tokens.notes: Distinct from search (traditional keyword search engine) and ai-input (live inference). Covers the pre-processing step of converting content into embeddings or other representations for AI retrieval systems. Covered by ai-all.

tokens.description: Traditional search engine indexing: crawling and displaying content in keyword search results.
tokens.notes: Covers web crawling for inclusion in non-AI search indexes (Google, Bing, DuckDuckGo, etc.). Distinct from ai-index (AI retrieval) and crawl (generic fetch without implicit downstream use).

tokens.description: Fetch and download content to create a local copy for any processing purpose.
tokens.notes: The most basic access function — does not imply any specific downstream use. Alias scrape is used in the IETF AIPREF context. RSL also uses crawl as a payment type (per-fetch billing); when used as a function token, it describes the access act, not the billing model.

tokens.description: Automated computational analysis of text and data: statistical analysis, pattern extraction, corpus research.
tokens.notes: Defined by EU Directive on Copyright (DSM Directive) Art. 4 as a permitted research exception unless opted out. Alias tdm is the common abbreviation. Broader than ai-train — TDM covers any automated analysis, not just ML training.

tokens.description: Text-to-speech synthesis: use content as the basis for audio rendering.
tokens.notes: Covers voice assistant reading, audiobook generation, and similar spoken-audio outputs from text content. Distinct from ai-input (inference) and stream (distribution of audio). Covered by ai-all.

tokens.description: Any use in a commercial context or for commercial gain.
tokens.notes: Creative Commons NC licenses restrict this. prohibited:[commercial] expresses CC-BY-NC semantics. Distinct from advertising (a specific commercial subtype). Does not automatically subsume advertising — publishers who want to prohibit both must list both.

tokens.description: Use in advertising, promotional, or marketing materials.
tokens.notes: A subtype of commercial. Editorial/news organizations may permit commercial use while prohibiting advertising. critical=true strongly recommended because misclassification creates direct infringement liability for the publisher.

tokens.description: Editorial, journalistic, or news reporting use.
tokens.notes: Distinct from commercial. Many stock media licenses permit editorial use (illustrating news stories) while prohibiting commercial/advertising use. critical=true strongly recommended.

tokens.description: Academic, scientific, or non-commercial research.
tokens.notes: Implies non-commercial and non-redistributive use. For commercial research entities that need explicit commercial permission, combine with commercial in permitted[].

tokens.description: Make copies of the work, digital or physical.
tokens.notes: The fundamental reproduction right under copyright law. Covers format conversion, digital copies, and print reproduction. Required for any use that involves stored copies of the content.

tokens.description: Distribute copies of the work to third parties.
tokens.notes: The distribution right under copyright law. Triggers copyleft SHARE_ALIKE obligations in GPL and CC-BY-SA when derivatives are distributed. Does not cover public performance or broadcasting.

tokens.description: Create derivative works, adaptations, or translations.
tokens.notes: The adaptation right under copyright law. Triggers SHARE_ALIKE obligations under CC-BY-SA and GPL when the derivative is also distributed. Covers translations, abridgements, musical arrangements, and transformations.

tokens.description: Publicly display the work on screen.
tokens.notes: Used in stock media (images, video stills) for on-screen display rights. Distinct from reproduce (making copies), broadcast (over-the-air/cable), and stream (on-demand internet delivery).

tokens.description: Synchronize the work with audio-visual media (synchronization license).
tokens.notes: Music industry standard term for pairing music with video (film, TV, YouTube, ads). A separate sync license is required in addition to any mechanical or master use license. critical=true strongly recommended.

tokens.description: Broadcast the work over radio, television, or similar over-the-air or cable transmission.
tokens.notes: Distinct from stream (on-demand internet delivery) and display (static screen display). Requires a performing rights license in most jurisdictions (ASCAP, BMI, SESAC for music; similar bodies for other works).

tokens.description: Deliver the work via on-demand internet streaming.
tokens.notes: Covers music streaming services (Spotify, Apple Music), video-on-demand (Netflix, YouTube), and podcast distribution. Distinct from broadcast (over-the-air/cable) and display (static rendering).

tokens.description: Reproduce the work in print media: newspapers, books, magazines, posters.
tokens.notes: Distinct from display (screen rendering) and reproduce (general copying). Covers physical print production and print-on-demand.

tokens.description: Manufacture physical goods from or incorporating the licensed design, invention, or pattern.
tokens.notes: Core patent right: making physical embodiments of a patented invention or protected design. Use with Quota metric units-manufactured to cap total production. OFFLINE_SELF_REPORTED metering typically required since the Exchange cannot observe manufacturing events.

tokens.description: Sell goods or services incorporating or based on the licensed work.
tokens.notes: The sale right in patent law, distinct from the distribution right in copyright (which covers copies of expressive works, not goods embodying a patented invention). Typically paired with manufacture. First-sale doctrine applies differently across jurisdictions.
